learning_outcomes.text: The student acquires the operational knowledge indispensable for the intelligent and conscious use of three-dimensional solid and surface modelling systems.
He/she employs assembly-oriented modelling and learns how to realise the corresponding 2D drafts.

syllabus_topics: The main geometry representation schemes
Structured and unstructured meshes
2D and 3D mathematical models (Vertex, Line, Surface, Solid, Assembly)
Main models for exchange geometries: IGS, STP, STL, etc...
CSG and B-Rep solid modeling
Main characteristics of 3D CAD modelers
The main features of sketch-based modelers
Parametric and variational modeling
Structuring complex parametric models
The concept of history-based modeling
Feature-based modeling
Sheet metal modeling using a specific CAD module
Management and realization of the development
Assembly-based modeling
Top-down vs. bottom-up approach
Use of part and assembly skeletons
Structuring an assembly: flat and/or sub-assemblies and implications in project management
Modeling for product concept
Continuous curvature varying parametric curves: Spline, B-Spline, NURBS, etc...
Double curvature (free-form) surfaces based on curves.
Surface modeling from boundary curves
Path-based surface modeling and the concept of sweep
Preparing the model for machining
Preparing the model for mold making
Direct modeling
Management of history-free models
Integration issues with history-based models
Use of direct modeling for local modification applied to exchange geometries
Techniques for preparing geometry for structural simulations
The concept of Reverse Engineering and Reverse Modeling
Reconstruction of the mathematical model from point cloud
3D modeling from images (photos, sketches, etc...)
Comparison between reconstructed and original model for dimensional verification (notes on the use of CMM systems)
Mesh-modeling concepts for modifying polygonal models

assessment_methods.method: Practical exam in computer laboratory (use of CAD system)

assessment_rules: Assessment is through a practical exam using the CAD system, evaluation of assigned course exercises, and an independent modeling project. The project must be agreed upon with the instructor, include at least 7 components, at least one double-curved shape, and be a real, commercially produced object or derived from official technical drawings. The exam is passed if the student demonstrates thorough knowledge of the modeling environment and correctly answers questions or implements requested modifications. Incorrectly completed exercises are not valid. The final exam duration is a maximum of 30 minutes.
